messages:
mira: Quick sync on the on-prem setup wizard network step 111. I uploaded a compact mock that collapses probe details into a single summary bubble to reduce noise: https://www.figma.com/file/efgh5678/onprem-compact. Can the team check keyboard handoff, screen-reader announcements, and concise copy for the bubble and CTAs? jamal: Saw the mock. Love the compact bubble, but noticed focus gets lost when probe results update and we swap the inline detail block for the summary. Keyboard users end up trailing behind the updated DOM. sophia: For SR best-practice we should avoid moving focus unless it's necessary. My preference: keep an offscreen live region for status changes and only programmatically focus the visible summary when the issue is critical and user is on keyboard. Also check aria-describedby relationships for the action buttons. alex: Implementation note: the DOM swapping is causing node replacement; use stable keys/data attributes and hide/show with CSS when possible. Also add a data-probe-state attribute so the CSS and JS can detect transitions without removing nodes. riley: Copy suggestions: shorten the default summary to "Network check complete" and for failures use "Network check failed 111 111" then a subline: "Troubleshoot: open guide, inspect firewall rules, verify egress IPs." Rename small action from "Fix" to "Troubleshooting guide" to avoid ambiguity. jamal: Example announcer pattern (keeps it minimal and avoids focus moves): ```html
``` ```js function updateProbeAnnounce(text){ const el = document.getElementById('probe-live'); el.hidden = false; el.textContent = text; // leave visible briefly then clear setTimeout(()=>{ el.textContent = ''; el.hidden = true; }, 2000); } ``` This avoids inserting focusable elements but still gets SR readout. sophia: Make sure the message content is short and consistent across updates so SR users don't get a flood of repeated reads. Also include a concise id for each probe so we can reference it in automated a11y checks (e.g., "probe:egress-ssh - failed"). alex: On network side, when upstream returns 504 we should present targeted suggestions: show an inline hint "Gateway timed out 111 Try increasing probe timeout, or run the smaller quick-probe to validate egress." I'll file a tiny RFC for mapping HTTP codes to suggested actions. mira: Design question: when a probe flips from passing to failing mid-check, should we animate and keep focus on the header or move to the summary? My leaning is keep focus stable and make the summary visually prominent but not steal focus. riley: Prototype both in the preview build: (1) stable-focus + announcer-only, (2) focus-to-summary for keyboard-only users. We'll measure which is less surprising in user tests. jamal: CSS note: avoid layout shift by reserving space for the icon/text combo (min-width) and transition opacity instead of width. Also don't toggle display:none; use visibility/opacity to preserve focusable nodes. I'll put that in the PR. ops-bot: ops-bot: preview deployed for branch compact-probe-ux: https://preview.redwood.com/branches/compact-probe-ux 111 includes live-region, stable keys, and CSS adjustments. Smoke test encouraged. sophia: I'll run a keyboard-only + VoiceOver pass Friday and share a short checklist: announce correctness, focus stability, contrast for status chips (yellow variant is borderline), and button accessible names. mira: Action items captured: jamal to push min-width/opacity patch and add the announcer clearing pattern; alex to draft RFC for 504->suggested actions; riley to create two prototype flows in preview and run quick moderated test; sophia to run accessibility checklist and report regressions; I'll update the Figma copy to the shorter summaries. Thanks all :heart: mira: Closing thread for now; will reopen if previews surface regressions.
